quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When can you cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?

options.text: The vehicle in front of you moves to the right to let you pass.
The yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
The yellow line on the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass if it is safe. A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. You must look over your shoulders to check them.

questions.question: What should you do when driving near a large truck?

options.text: Follow it closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Do not drive beside it for long periods of time.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside it for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots on both sides. Avoid driving beside them for long periods.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: Anything that causes you to take evasive action while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving means your eyes, hands, or mind are not on the road. It is a major cause of crashes because drivers miss important visual and audio cues.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Speed up so you do not cause an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam lights in fog and slow down. If fog is too thick to see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: What does this sign show?

options.text: The height from the road to a bridge or overpass.
The maximum legal height for vehicles in this state.
The maximum width for vehicles on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The height from the road to a bridge or overpass.
questions.explanation: This is a low clearance warning sign. It shows the distance from the road to the bottom of a bridge or overpass.

questions.question: What are bicycles considered when used on roadways?

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles on roadways. Bicycle riders and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
No left turn.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn left. Making a left turn at this intersection is unsafe and against the law.

questions.question: When there are no signs or lane markings at an intersection, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The first available lane.
The last available lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The first available lane.
questions.explanation: Turn into the first legal lane in your direction of travel. This prevents collisions caused by changing lanes while turning.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line mean?

options.text: Vehicles in both directions may pass.
Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you may pass.

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing a vehicle?

options.text: When the driver you passed signals for you to return.
When you signal for three seconds.
When you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, you have enough distance to return to your lane safely.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the center mean?

options.text: Reduce your speed.
A traffic light is ahead.
Do not pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means passing is not allowed. Solid lines on both sides also mean no passing from either direction.

questions.question: What headlights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back and make it harder to see.

questions.question: You are on the freeway and traffic is merging into your lane. You should:

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.
Assert your right-of-way by driving faster.
Always maintain your position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.
questions.explanation: When it is safe, make room for vehicles to merge into your lane.

questions.question: When driving on the highway, looking far ahead of your vehicle:

options.text: Helps you keep up with traffic.
Reduces the need for sudden braking or turning.
Allows you to spot upcoming police officers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduces the need for sudden braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Looking far ahead helps you avoid sudden braking or turning. You can prepare early, drive safely, save fuel, and keep traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, use:

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect back and create glare that makes it hard to see.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: School crossing.
School zone.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a crosswalk. Watch for pedestrians crossing the road.

questions.question: In which situation should your wheels not be pointed straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
questions.explanation: When waiting to turn left, keep wheels straight so a rear-end hit won't push you into oncoming traffic. On a hill, turn wheels so the car won't roll into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: After you pass a vehicle, it is safe to move back into the right lane:

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can return to your lane when you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection at the posted speed limit when the signal turns yellow. You should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed through the intersection without caution.
Speed up to cross the intersection before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will soon turn red. Stop if you can do so safely. Otherwise, cross the intersection with caution.

questions.question: The amount of alcohol in the blood is called:

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC means more impairment.

questions.question: A yellow traffic light warns that the light will turn red soon. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.
Increase your speed so as not to cause an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through and clear the intersection as quickly as possible.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
You should always brake hard to ensure stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Apply the brakes gently with steady pressure so your vehicle stops smoothly.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a downhill ramp that curves. You should:

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
Wait until you have entered the curve to begin braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You cannot see ahead clearly, and braking in a curve can cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: When stopped at a red light with a green arrow, you may proceed in the arrow direction if:

options.text: You first come to a complete stop.
You wait until the light changes.
You are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You can proceed in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear. Always yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.
